title: Progressive regional failover canary with token-admit heatmap and circuit grace dashboard
creator: Asha Kothari
description: Build a canary and observability surface that validates progressive multi-region failover behavior while surfacing token-level admission and circuit grace behavior. The goal is to detect regressions in SLO enforcement and load-shedding logic before they affect production traffic and to provide a concise on-call dashboard that shows region-by-region admit rates, token-latency SLIs, circuit states, and the ‘grace’ window behavior for circuit breakers during transient overloads. This ticket covers instrumentation, dashboard panels, synthetic canary traffic generation, and a short rollout plan for gradual monitoring-driven failover tests.
acceptance_criteria: A Grafana dashboard exists with region-by-region panels for token admit rate, token p50/p95/p99 latency, and per-region circuit state with last transition timestamps.

A canary job (k8s CronJob + synthetic harness) can exercise per-region failover progressively (region A -> B partial -> B full) without impacting customer traffic and publishes synthetic traces to the same telemetry pipeline.
Token-level SLI calculation verified: admit_rate and token_p95 align with production sampling (sampling rate documented) and computed in real-time with under 30s latency.

Circuit grace behavior visible: when a circuit opens, dashboard shows a configurable grace window slider and corresponding synthetic failure traces demonstrating graceful degradation and automatic re-accept attempts.
Runbook section for the dashboard describing common alarms (e.g., sustained drop in admit_rate, p99 spike with KV hit ratio drop) and immediate mitigations is attached to the ticket.
Unit/integration tests for the synthetic traffic harness and telemetry enrichment exist and run in CI; PR linked and merged.
implementation_notes: Instrument token admit path to emit admit_rate events with region, shard, customer_tier, and admit_reason tags; sample at 1% for high-volume paths and 100% for canary requests.
Compute token-level SLIs using streaming aggregator that supports sliding windows (60s, 5m) and outputs p50/p95/p99 histograms and quantile summaries to metrics backend.
Add lightweight circuit state events to control plane stream: {circuit_id, region, state, reason, opened_at, closed_at, grace_window_ms} so dashboards can calculate time-in-state.
Dashboard should join metrics with synthetic trace IDs for drilldown to k/v cache hit rates, batching sizes, and kernel selection tags to attribute latency sources.
Prefer existing metric names to minimize migration: use redwood.token_admit.rate, redwood.token_latency.hist, redwood.circuit.state_event; add tags where missing (region, shard, model_family).
dashboard_panels: Global summary: overall token admit_rate (1m, 5m) with trend and annotation feed for canary events.
Region grid: admit_rate, p95 token latency, p99 token latency for each active region (small multiples).
Circuit map: list of circuits with current state, time-in-state, and last transition reason; filter by model_family and customer_tier.
Token-admit heatmap: 2D heatmap where X axis = time of day, Y axis = token length bucket, color = admit_rate drop; per-region toggle.
Grace window visualizer: when a circuit opens show a timeline of automatic re-admit attempts and success ratio during configured grace_window_ms.
Synthetic canary lane: canary job success/failure, end-to-end latency, and synthetic trace links; overlay with production anomalies.
KV-cache correlation panel: token p95 vs kv_hit_rate with correlation coefficient and scatter plot to highlight cache-related latency modes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement metric emission and local dashboard; verify synthetic job emits expected payloads (dev cluster).
Phase 1 (staging): deploy canary job targeting staging regions; validate dashboard panels and SLI computations with synthetic failures injected (chaos).
Phase 2 (gradual prod): enable read-only dashboard in prod, run canary traffic at 0.1% of prod QPS for 48h; verify no customer impact and alarms behave.
Phase 3 (monitoring-driven): activate automated playback of canary scenario weekly and enable alerting thresholds for token p95 and admit_rate drops.
test_plan: Unit tests for the streaming aggregator and sliding-window quantile code (CI).
Integration test that runs synthetic canary in ephemeral env and asserts dashboard metrics appear within 60s.
Chaos test in staging that simulates KV cache eviction and validates that token latency/p99 and admit_rate panels show expected regression signatures.
Load test for metric emission pipeline to ensure additional instrumentation adds <5% CPU overhead under 2x baseline QPS.
